κρᾰται-ίς , ἡ, (κρατύς) of the stone of Sisyphus, ὅτε μέλλοι ἄκρον ὑπερβαλέειν, τότ᾽ ἀποστρέψασκε κραταιίς when it was just about to surmount the top, then did
A.mighty weight turn it back, dub. in Od. 11.597 (taken as Adv., violently, by Aristarch. ; as κράται᾽ ἴς (where κράταια may be an old fem. of κρατύς like *πλάταια (cf. Skt. pṛthivī), pl. Πλαταιαί, fem. of πλατύς) by Ptol.Asc. ap. Hdn.Gr. 2.153 ).
II. (proparox.) as pr.n., the Mighty one, name of the mother of Scylla,
Od. 12.124 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
